title: Lean 4 Proof Replay Tool: Checking Reproducibility of Published LLM Verification Results

original_idea.body:
# Lean 4 Proof Replay Tool: Checking Reproducibility of Published LLM Verification Results

**Problem:** Published results for Lean 4 proof generation are difficult to reproduce because proof checker behavior can vary across Lean 4 versions. No standardized reproduction protocol exists for formal verification LLM benchmarks.

**Direction:** Develop a lightweight reproduction protocol: (a) standardize Lean 4 version, (b) containerized evaluation environment, (c) automated re-run of published VeriBench results with 3 models. Measure result stability across Lean 4 minor versions (1.1 vs 1.2 vs 1.3). Document discrepancies.

**Why it matters:** Reproducibility is a prerequisite for science. Lean 4's active development means proofs that compile on one version may not compile on another. A standardized protocol prevents benchmark inflation through version selection.

**Relevant context:** Lean 4 is under active development. Mathlib proofs break during Lean upgrades. VeriBench was evaluated on a specific Lean version. No reproduction kit exists. This is infrastructure for the field.
